en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having a nearly perfect cone shape of any active volcano worldwide.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines, flowing through five provinces.
Taal Lake in Batangas is the third largest lake in the Philippines and contains Volcano Island within its waters.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippine eagle, found in the forests of Mindanao and Luzon, is one of the largest and rarest eagles globally.
The Rafflesia, found in the rainforests of Luzon and Visayas, produces the largest individual flower in the world.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected sanctuary for diverse and vibrant coral reefs.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, containing the capital city of Manila.
The Philippines experiences the amihan or northeast monsoon, which brings cool and dry air from November to February.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over two thousand years ago.
